To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
The cotton plant is a host for many insects, including the bollworm, and the plant’s resistance to the bollworm can be enhanced by breeding for certain morphological and biochemical traits.
the cotton cultivar, G 27 was resistant to bollworms, while, the cotton cultivars, NA360, NA 362, NA 363 and NA 364 were susceptible to bollworm infestations.

1) the cotton cultivar, NA 360 was found to be highly susceptible to the bollworms, while the cultivars G 28, Eknath and Rohini were found to be highly resistant, 2) the bollworm infestations were significantly higher on shed material and fruit body of the plant than on the vegetative part of the plant, 3) the boll rind and tannin were negatively associated with the bollworm attack,
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of the morphological and chemical characters of cotton that are associated with resistance to the bollworms, and the genetic control of these characters.
the identification and evaluation of resistance mechanisms against cotton bollworm, Helicoverpa armigera (Hübner) in cotton genotypes.
the identification and characterization of a new class of compounds that have the potential to be used as a novel class of antiviral drugs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the cultivars G 227, Eknath and Rohini were found to be resistant to bollworms.
the cultivar G 27, which is rich in hair density, nitrogen content of leaf, tannin content of boll and boll rind, is the most suitable cultivar for bollworm resistance.
cultivars, which have higher hair density, higher nitrogen content of leaf, lower boll rind, thickness and lower tannin content, would be resistant to cotton bollworms.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the cultivars G 28, Eknath and Rohini are resistant to cotton bollworms and the cultivar PA 141 is susceptible to bollworms.
, the bollworm resistance is positively related to the leaf hair density, boll rind and boll wall thickness, while negatively associated with bolls per plant.
cotton cultivars with high hair density, high nitrogen content of leaf, low boll rind and low tannin contents of boll are more resistant to cotton bollworms.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the bollworm infests the cotton plants at different stages of its development, and the plant’s response to the infestation is also variable.
we have a new biomarker for resistance, namely, hair density of leaf and nitrogen content of leaves.
we have developed a new method to study the evolution of resistance to a major pest in a wild crop relative, and that this method can be used to identify the genetic basis of this resistance.
